caption: Figure 2: Self-distillation with no labels. We illustrate DINO in the case of one single pair of views ( x 1 , x 2 ) for simplicity. The model passes two different random transformations of an input image to the student and teacher networks. Both networks have the same architecture but different parameters. The output of the teacher network is centered with a mean computed over the batch. Each networks outputs a K dimensional feature that is normalized with a temperature softmax over the feature dimension. Their similarity is then measured with a cross-entropy loss. We apply a stop-gradient (sg) operator on the teacher to propagate gradients only through the student. The teacher parameters are updated with an exponential moving average (ema) of the student parameters.
description:
Figure type: Diagram
Description: The diagram illustrates the self-distillation process in DINO, a self-supervised learning method for vision transformers. It shows a single pair of input views (x1, x2) being processed by a student network (gθs) and a teacher network (gθt). Both networks have the same architecture but different parameters. The student network outputs a feature vector, which is normalized using a softmax function. The teacher network also outputs a feature vector, which is centered using a mean computed over the batch. The similarity between the student and teacher outputs is measured using a cross-entropy loss. The teacher parameters are updated with an exponential moving average (ema) of the student parameters.
